paths.description: Homepage and shared public brochure template; represents key-benefit and marketing content routes.
Delivers More Reservations page; representative second instance of the shared informational template.
System-status archetype; highest-risk public operational state surface.
Primary account-entry form and password authentication surface; audited without credentials.
Unknown-route recovery state used to judge HTTP failure handling.

Authenticated property-management screens, successful sign-in, password reset, the PDF body, and destructive/account flows were not covered because credentials or non-HTML document interaction were unavailable; representative public templates were de-duplicated.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture; the probe reports colorScheme "normal" and no preference media rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light/dark color schemes before paint and use preference-driven surface and text colors.

findings.summary: Transitions do not account for reduced-motion preference.
findings.evidence: CSS applies 0.2s hover transitions while the reduced-motion probe found no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential transitions in no-preference and provide a reduced-motion override.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or @view-transition rule across the informational MPA routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Section navigation does not indicate the current page.
findings.evidence: The CSS defines .nav a.active, but rendered home and delivers DOM never apply it, so all links look equivalent.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply aria-current="page" and a persistent visual current-page treatment.

findings.summary: The public and login pages ship a desktop canvas to mobile.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360px viewport, Chrome lays out a 980px page at scale 0.367 because viewport meta is absent; CSS enforces min-width:980px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a viewport meta tag, remove fixed minimum widths, and recompose navigation/content into a true single-column mobile layout.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no container queries; header, hero, login card, nav and wrapper use fixed widths and global breakpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable regions containment and use size container queries for local layout changes.

findings.summary: Failure and invalid states offer no actionable recovery.
findings.evidence: Blank login submission produced no visible error, and an unknown URL returns the raw Apache 404 with no navigation, retry, or support path.
findings.suggestedFix: Add inline, announced validation and a branded error page with clear recovery actions.

findings.summary: Resource delivery has avoidable broken and unprioritised dependencies.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse logged two 404 font requests, a cache-control:no-store BFCache blocker, and no fetchpriority hint on the hero LCP image; LCP was still 2.0s.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix font URLs, apply deliberate caching/BFCache policy, and mark the LCP image fetchpriority="high" with dimensions.

findings.summary: Third-party and login bundles ship substantial unused code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 38 KiB unused in Boomerang; login also shipped 27 KiB unused first-party JS and 14 KiB of 94% unused Bootstrap CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load telemetry and trim the login bundle/CSS to the controls used.

findings.summary: Images and login controls lack accessible names and associations.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found all four public-page images missing alt; Lighthouse found both login inputs without associated labels and an unnamed footer link.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful or empty alt text, explicitly associate labels and inputs, and name every interactive link.

findings.summary: Text and navigation fail WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured public nav links at 4.36:1 and login labels at 3.54:1; the login footer was 2.34:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken low-contrast text/links or adjust backgrounds to meet at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

findings.summary: Pages lack robust semantic structure.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark on public and login pages; public HTML has only presentation role markup. Native focus outlines are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use header/nav/main/footer landmarks and preserve the currently visible native focus treatment.

findings.summary: Core copy is too small and faint for comfortable reading.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS uses 13px #999 body text and an 11px #d3d3d3 footer; screenshots show low-emphasis text across long content.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise base text size/line height and use stronger text colors and comfortable line lengths.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow is disabled by the missing viewport configuration.
findings.evidence: The 360px audit is rendered as a scaled 980px desktop page, making text and controls physically small despite no CSS overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore 1:1 mobile viewport scaling and implement true reflow without fixed minimum widths.

findings.summary: The page logs resource errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured two 404 errors for Sansation regular and bold font URLs.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the font paths and add monitoring that catches production asset 404s.

findings.summary: The public document is in quirks mode and has malformed asset metadata.
findings.evidence: The probe reports no doctype and BackCompat; DOM shows conflicting UTF-8 and ISO-8859-1 declarations, while images lack dimensions and the hero has a mismatched aspect ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a valid HTML5 doctype, one early UTF-8 charset, and explicit intrinsic image dimensions/aspect ratios.

findings.summary: Deprecated lifecycle code and cache policy block modern browser behavior.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a deprecated unload listener in Boomerang and BFCache failure from no-store plus a subframe unload handler.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or defer the telemetry library, remove unload handlers, and use BFCache-compatible lifecycle events and caching where safe.

findings.summary: Public pages have generic duplicate titles and no descriptions.
findings.evidence: Home and delivers both use "ChoiceADVANTAGE.com"; Lighthouse reports no meta description on home or login.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each route a unique descriptive title and concise, content-matching meta description.

findings.summary: Crawler-visible pages are not mobile friendly.
findings.evidence: Links are real hrefs and raw-HTML coverage is 99%, but the public page omits viewport meta and renders a 980px layout on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep crawlable links and add mobile viewport/reflow support.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Recon found /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return 404, and the DOM has no canonical or robots metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish robots.txt and sitemap.xml, add self-referential canonicals, and keep HTTP/indexing policy consistent.

findings.summary: The organization pages lack structured and social metadata.
findings.evidence: The probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph metadata despite visible Choice Hotels product/organization content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/SoftwareApplication JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but CSP is absent; the public route lacks nosniff and RT/ROUTEID cookies are not Secure with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP, nosniff, and secure/Lax-or-Strict cookie attributes unless cross-site behavior is essential.

findings.summary: Telemetry loads before any demonstrated user need or consent context.
findings.evidence: Trackers evidence records two mPulse origins; HAR attributes 59,280 bytes and two requests to third parties, with Boomerang mostly unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Document the telemetry purpose, minimise fields, defer/batch it, and load it only where proportionate.

findings.summary: The account entry offers password-only authentication.
findings.evidence: Login DOM contains only username/password fields, disables autocomplete, and the probe found no WebAuthn or navigator.credentials integration.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey sign-in/registration and retain a secure fallback; request any permissions only after a user action.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Both routes omit CSP, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; clickjacking and HSTS are present, and the public route omits nosniff.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a nonce/hash-based CSP with frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy, least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and nosniff.

findings.summary: The app-like account surface has no installable/offline experience.
findings.evidence: The probe found no web app manifest; the only registration is Akamai’s telemetry/service worker and no user-facing offline fallback was evidenced.
findings.suggestedFix: For the operational account app, add a manifest and a minimal offline/reconnect shell; keep auth operations online-only.

findings.summary: HTTP failures fall through to server-default output.
findings.evidence: The tested unknown route shows a raw Apache 2.4.58 404 with no branded navigation or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an accessible 404/error template with home, status, support, and retry options.

findings.summary: Language and bidirectional foundations are absent on key routes.
findings.evidence: Public and login DOM report no html lang; CSS inspection found no logical properties and relies on left/right positioning.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang and dir, replace physical spacing/positioning with logical properties, and test translated/RTL expansion.

findings.summary: The login form neither prevents nor explains blank submission.
findings.evidence: Inputs are not required, lack associated labels, and clicking Login with empty values left the same screen with no visible or announced error.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required semantics, validate after interaction, focus the error summary, and associate clear inline messages with each field.

findings.summary: Sign-in deliberately disables password-manager and autofill assistance.
findings.evidence: Both username and password inputs use autocomplete="off"; the username field is not identified as username and the password as current-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="username" and "current-password", stable ids/names, and do not block paste or password managers.

findings.summary: Account recovery and stronger authentication are not self-service.
findings.evidence: The login says users who forgot a password must contact support and exposes no passkey or account-management entry point.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer clear self-service recovery and passkeys, while keeping commitments and account actions reversible and reauthenticated.

findings.summary: Images are not delivered responsively or in modern formats.
findings.evidence: All four public images are PNG/JPEG; three lack srcset, all lack dimensions, and Lighthouse flags low-resolution logos on high-density displays.
findings.suggestedFix: Use SVG/AVIF/WebP as appropriate, responsive srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions, and a correctly cropped hero source.

findings.summary: Third-party telemetry consumes a disproportionate share of a small page.
findings.evidence: HAR totals 293,468 transferred bytes; 59,280 bytes are third-party, and Lighthouse estimates 38 KiB of Boomerang is unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or remove nonessential telemetry and enforce a small third-party budget for this brochure surface.
